_why:
#37 — the carried row's FACTS hold and its PRESCRIPTION is refused, which is the sixth time this session's lane has hit that shape. A slot quoted in prose backticks does trip the advisory; the probe's suggested cure ('the fix worth having, if any, is backtick awareness') would blind the detector on the one template that needs it most.

Measured across every `h-mad/**/*.md` carrying a slot: `codex-verifier-prompt.md` has 17 BACKTICKED live slots and 1 bare, because they are written into prose sentences. SKILL.md records that the assembler does not stage that template, so hand-shipping is its only route -- exactly the unguarded path this advisory exists for. Stripping backticked spans takes it from 18 detected slots to 1.

This spec has ONE mutation on purpose. It is not a guard over new behaviour -- nothing in the script changed -- it is a guard over a REFUSAL, and the only way that refusal can be undone is by someone implementing the thing it refuses. So the mutation IS the proposed fix, written out in full.

mutations.name: backtick-awareness-is-implemented-as-proposed
mutations._mechanism: The #37 prescription, verbatim: strip backticked spans before the grep. `codex-verifier-prompt.md` then reports 1 live slot instead of 18, and a hand-shipped 5e verifier prompt with seventeen unsubstituted slots dispatches near-silently -- the agent reviews placeholders and the reply reads like a real verification.
mutations.find:
if grep -qE '<INLINE[^>]*>|<REPORT_FILE_PATH>|<AUDIT_SENTINEL>' "$promptfile" 2>/dev/null; then
    local _slots
    _slots=$(grep -oE '<INLINE[^>]*>|<REPORT_FILE_PATH>|<AUDIT_SENTINEL>' "$promptfile" \
             | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
mutations.replace:
if sed 's/`[^`]*`//g' "$promptfile" | grep -qE '<INLINE[^>]*>|<REPORT_FILE_PATH>|<AUDIT_SENTINEL>' 2>/dev/null; then
    local _slots
    _slots=$(sed 's/`[^`]*`//g' "$promptfile" | grep -oE '<INLINE[^>]*>|<REPORT_FILE_PATH>|<AUDIT_SENTINEL>' \
             | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
